skill.name: cookbook-audit
skill.description: Audits Anthropic Cookbook Jupyter notebooks with an automated validator and a structured style rubric.
skill.summary: Review Anthropic Cookbook notebooks for structure, code quality, security hygiene, and learning value.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, cookbook examples, or benign documentation links. I confirmed the detect-secrets command path in validate_notebook.py because it builds sh -c pipelines with interpolated paths. No prompt injection or additional intent-level abuse was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace sh -c pipelines with direct subprocess argument arrays and pass notebook paths as separate arguments to detect-secrets-hook.

remediation.issue: Unsafe path interpolation in detect-secrets commands
remediation.suggestion: Avoid echo and xargs for notebook paths. Add tests for paths containing quotes, spaces, and shell metacharacters.
Pin versions for nbconvert and detect-secrets tooling so validation behavior is reproducible across environments.

content.value_statement: Cookbook notebooks can drift from style, setup, and security standards before review. This skill combines automated checks with a rubric-based content audit.
actual_capabilities: Reads the included style guide before reviewing a cookbook notebook.
Runs a validator that converts notebooks to markdown for easier review.
Checks introductions, prerequisites, setup, conclusions, and code explanations.
Scans notebook content for possible hardcoded secrets when tooling is available.
Scores narrative quality, code quality, technical accuracy, and actionability.
Produces prioritized recommendations with concrete notebook references.
limitations: It is tuned for Anthropic Cookbook standards, not every notebook style.
It requires a local notebook path and working Python command-line tools.
Automated checks do not replace manual technical review.
It may miss project-specific requirements outside the rubric.

use_cases.title: Review a Cookbook Pull Request
use_cases.description: Apply the rubric to a submitted notebook and return a clear score with required fixes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Notebook for Submission
use_cases.description: Find missing setup details, weak introductions, noisy outputs, and unclear code explanations before review.

use_cases.title: Check Security and Model Hygiene
use_cases.description: Scan for possible secrets, dated model IDs, invalid model names, and weak environment setup practices.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Notebook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with a provided notebook path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Anthropic Cookbook notebook: <path>. Run the automated validator, review the markdown output, and give a score with the top fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Learning Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review focused on teaching effectiveness.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review <path> for narrative quality and actionability. Check the introduction, learning objectives, explanations before code, and conclusion mapping.

prompt_templates.title: Check Technical Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review focused on implementation details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit <path> for technical accuracy, setup quality, model naming, dependency handling, output management, and possible hardcoded secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Against the Full Rubric
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full cookbook audit for <path>. Score all four dimensions, cite specific notebook sections, separate blockers from suggestions, and propose exact revisions.

output_examples.input: Audit a notebook that lacks learning objectives and has noisy installation output.
output_examples.output: The report gives a lower narrative and actionability score, flags missing objectives, recommends suppressed installation output, and lists publication blockers first.

output_examples.input: Review a notebook that uses a dated Claude model ID and a weak conclusion.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the dated model issue, suggests a supported alias, and asks for a conclusion that maps back to stated learning objectives.

output_examples.input: Check a cookbook draft before opening a pull request.
output_examples.output: The report summarizes readiness, lists the strongest sections, and gives prioritized edits for setup, explanations, examples, and security hygiene.

best_practices: Run the automated validator before the manual rubric review.
Cite specific notebook cells or sections when giving recommendations.
Separate critical publication blockers from optional quality improvements.
anti_patterns: Scoring a notebook without reading the style guide first.
Treating automated checks as a complete content review.
Giving generic feedback without concrete notebook references.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits Anthropic Cookbook Jupyter notebooks against a style guide, validation checks, and a four-part scoring rubric.

faq.question: Does it run code inside the notebook?
faq.answer: The validator converts notebooks to markdown and inspects cells. It is not designed to execute notebook cells.

faq.question: Can it detect hardcoded secrets?
faq.answer: It attempts to run detect-secrets and also includes fallback pattern checks for common API key formats.

faq.question: What score does it produce?
faq.answer: It scores narrative quality, code quality, technical accuracy, and actionability for a total out of 20.

faq.question: Can I use it for non-Anthropic notebooks?
faq.answer: You can, but the recommendations are based on Anthropic Cookbook standards and may not fit other formats.

faq.question: What should I provide to start?
faq.answer: Provide the local path to the notebook that needs review.
